title: In characteristic p, injectivity of H_1(L_{K/k}) -> m/m^2 gives injectivity of Omega_{k/F_p} (x) K -> Omega_{A/F_p} (x) K
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-pc-field-characteristic] and $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ a Noetherian local $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with residue field $K=A/\mathfrak m$; $k$, $A$, $K$ are $\mathbf F_p$-algebras. Let $\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $H_1(L_{K/k})$ and $H_1(L_{K/A})$ be the first homologies of the naive cotangent complexes of the canonical presentations $k[K]\to K$ and $A[K]\to K$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]; the inclusion $k[K]\to A[K]$ is a morphism of presentations over the square $k\to A$, $\mathrm{id}_K$, and so induces a $K$-linear map $H_1(L_{K/k})\to H_1(L_{K/A})$ [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]; the canonical map $\gamma:H_1(L_{K/k})\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is its composite with the isomorphism $H_1(L_{K/A})\cong\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1] for the surjection $A\to K$. Let $\lambda:\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_kK\to\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_AK$ be the $K$-linear map $\mathrm da\otimes x\mapsto\mathrm d(a\cdot1_A)\otimes x$. If $\gamma$ is injective, then $\lambda$ is injective.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular, line 8697), proof, paragraph 'Equivalence of (3) and (4)' (lines 8763-8795): the Jacobi-Zariski sequences of F_p -> A -> K and F_p -> k -> K, with H_1(L_{K/A}) = m/m^2 and H_1(L_{K/F_p}) = 0 (Algebra 0322), show that the kernels of H_1(L_{K/k}) -> m/m^2 and of Omega_{k/F_p} (x) K -> Omega_{A/F_p} (x) K have the same dimension; the direction (3) => (4) is stated here, without the regularity of A, which the argument does not use (tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags: 07E5,more-algebra-proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular)

proof.text: Bottom row (the Jacobi-Zariski sequence of $\mathbf F_p\to k\to K$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] with $A=\mathbf F_p$, $B=k$, $C=K$ and $\varphi:k\to K$ the structure map ($K=A/\mathfrak m$ is a $k$-algebra through $k\to A\to K$). Its exact sequence contains $$H_1(L_{K/k})\xrightarrow{\ \partial_k\ }K\otimes_k\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{\ w_k\ }\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p},\qquad w_k(x\otimes\mathrm ds)=x\,\mathrm d(s\cdot1_K),$$ exact at the middle term: $\ker w_k=\operatorname{im}\partial_k$. (This is the lower row of the source's diagram, read at $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_kK$; the identification $K\otimes_k\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\cong\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_kK$, $x\otimes\omega\mapsto\omega\otimes x$, is used silently below.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular), proof, paragraph 'Equivalence of (3) and (4)', lines 8763-8795, first diagram (lower row) and the Jacobi-Zariski sequence it produces (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2)

proof.text: Top row is injective on the left. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] with $A=\mathbf F_p$, $B=A$, $C=K$, $\varphi:A\to K$ the quotient map: the part $H_1(L_{K/\mathbf F_p})\xrightarrow{v_A}H_1(L_{K/A})\xrightarrow{\partial_A}K\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}$ is exact at $H_1(L_{K/A})$, so $\ker\partial_A=\operatorname{im}v_A$. The field $K$ receives the field $k$ of characteristic $p$, so $K$ has characteristic $p$ [def-pc-field-characteristic] and [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-h1-cotangent-vanishing] gives $H_1(L_{K/\mathbf F_p})=0$; hence $\partial_A$ is injective. By the case $S=B$ of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-connecting-map-naturality] (with $R=\mathbf F_p$, $B=A$, $I=\mathfrak m$, $C=K$) we have $\delta\circ\theta=\partial_A$, where $\theta:H_1(L_{K/A})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1] and $\delta:\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to K\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}$, $f\bmod\mathfrak m^2\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm df$. Since $\theta$ is bijective and $\partial_A$ injective, $\delta=\partial_A\circ\theta^{-1}$ is injective. (This is the upper row of the source's diagram, exact on the left because $H_1(L_{K/\mathbf F_p})=0$ by Algebra, Proposition Tag 0322, and with first term $H_1(L_{K/A})=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ by Algebra, Lemma Tag 07BP.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular), proof, paragraph 'Equivalence of (3) and (4)', lines 8763-8795, upper row of the second diagram; 'We have used that H_1(L_{K/A}) = m/m^2 and that H_1(L_{K/F_p}) = 0 as K/F_p is separable'

proof.text: The left square commutes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-connecting-map-naturality] with $R=\mathbf F_p$, $S=k$, $B=A$, $I=\mathfrak m$, $C=K$: with $\iota:H_1(L_{K/k})\to H_1(L_{K/A})$ the map induced by the morphism of presentations $k[K]\to A[K]$ over the square $k\to A$, $\mathrm{id}_K$ [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality], $\theta$ as in step 2, $\partial_k$ the connecting map of step 1, and $c:K\otimes_k\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\to K\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}$, $x\otimes\mathrm ds\mapsto x\otimes\mathrm d(s\cdot1_A)$, it gives $\delta\circ\theta\circ\iota=c\circ\partial_k$. By the definition in the statement, $\gamma=\theta\circ\iota$ (the same $\iota$ and the same $\theta$ of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1]), and $c$ is $\lambda$ after the identification of step 1 ($\lambda(\mathrm ds\otimes x)=\mathrm d(s\cdot1_A)\otimes x$). Hence $$\delta\circ\gamma=\lambda\circ\partial_k .$$

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular), proof, paragraph 'Equivalence of (3) and (4)', lines 8763-8795, second diagram, left square ('to get a commutative diagram')

proof.text: The middle square commutes: with $w_A:K\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$, $x\otimes\mathrm da\mapsto x\,\mathrm d\bar a$, the map $w$ of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] for $\mathbf F_p\to A\to K$ (the map $u$ of the source's upper row $\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_AK\to\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$), we have $w_A\circ\lambda=w_k$. Both sides are $K$-linear and, on the generators $x\otimes\mathrm ds$ ($x\in K$, $s\in k$), $w_A(\lambda(x\otimes\mathrm ds))=w_A(x\otimes\mathrm d(s\cdot1_A))=x\,\mathrm d(\overline{s\cdot1_A})=x\,\mathrm d(s\cdot1_K)=w_k(x\otimes\mathrm ds)$, since the image of $s\cdot1_A$ in $K=A/\mathfrak m$ is $s\cdot1_K$; the elements $\mathrm ds$ generate $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], so these generators span $K\otimes_k\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular), proof, paragraph 'Equivalence of (3) and (4)', lines 8763-8795, second diagram, middle square (the vertical arrow $\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$ is the identity)

proof.text: Diagram chase (direction (3) $\Rightarrow$ (4) of 'the kernels ... have the same dimension', written without dimensions). Let $x\in\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\otimes_kK$ with $\lambda(x)=0$. By step 4, $w_k(x)=w_A(\lambda(x))=0$, so by step 1 $x=\partial_k(h)$ for some $h\in H_1(L_{K/k})$. By step 3, $\delta(\gamma(h))=\lambda(\partial_k(h))=\lambda(x)=0$; $\delta$ is injective by step 2, so $\gamma(h)=0$; $\gamma$ is injective by hypothesis, so $h=0$ and $x=\partial_k(0)=0$. Hence $\lambda$ is injective. (The regularity of $A$ and the Noetherian hypothesis, present in (3) and (4) of 07E5, are not used.)
